Ours emits `fsubs f6,f0,f4` (the p[2]-C conversion) then `fsubs f5,f1,f3` (the p[0] conversion); the target emits them in the opposite order. Both are ready at +0x3c and their register ROLES already agree on both sides, so the transposition is the only thing breaking the bijection. THE GUARD REFUSAL WAS A FACT ABOUT THE GUARD, NOT THE FUNCTION (AGENTS discipline 14): webfrank_audit rejected with `+0x3c: use of f0 does not correspond to f2 under the running renaming`, and that refusal is generated by the transposition -- verify_consistent_recolor PASSES on the permuted body. It needs its per-def web handling to pass, because ours f1 maps to target f2 on the web defined at +0x34 and to target f3 on the disjoint web defined at +0x54; a global bijection would have failed here and the tool's dataflow in_maps is what makes it sound. The scheduler tie-break itself remains source-unreachable: the target picks the LESS ready of two ready fsubs at +0x3c (its lfd was issued 2 slots earlier at +0x34, while ours picks the operand ready since +0x2c), and no source form reaches that choice.
